alternative.claim: A minimal typed function-definition production can be added to the G9 grammar by reusing existing `needle_decl` (which already has params and return type) extended with an optional body expression, closing the definition→call gap without new semantic primitives.
alternative.counterhypothesis: The existing `rule`/`needle`/host-action surface already provides sufficient deterministic call-binding semantics to compile the mandatory application suite, making an explicit function-definition production redundant.
alternative.minimal_delta: Extend `needle_decl` with an optional `= expr` body clause: `needle_decl = 'needle', ident, '(', [params], ')', '->', type_expr, ['=', expr] ;`. Add a `FuncDef` node to canonical IR carrying (symbol_id, param_types, return_type, body_expr, effect_set). In the typechecker, resolve `call` targets against `FuncDef` symbol table with exact-identity match, arity check, and param-type compatibility; fail closed on any mismatch. No new keywords, no new nonterminals beyond the optional body.
alternative.executable_discriminator: Parse and compile a source file containing two typed function definitions with mutual calls (e.g., `needle is_even(n:Int)->Bool = n==0` and `needle is_odd(n:Int)->Bool = is_even(n-1)==false`), then execute 20,000 randomized calls through the canonical IR evaluator. Separately, attempt the same program using only existing `rule`/`needle` without body. If the existing surface cannot express a callable body with deterministic resolution, the counterhypothesis is rejected.
alternative.next_focus: Control-flow closure: independently close branching + loop/recursion + pattern match + structured Result/error semantics in the canonical IR, without bundling into the function-definition result.
